summary.text: Stratigraphy is the branch of geology that studies rock layers, called strata, and the way they are layered.
Layers in far-apart places holding the same fossils can be matched in time, and the geologic time scale was built on such fossil evidence in the 19th century.

facts.label: Missing layers
facts.value: A gap in the record is a stratigraphic hiatus

facts.label: Practical use
facts.value: Mapping oil-bearing reservoir rocks, seals and traps

items.prompt: Two cliffs hundreds of kilometres apart contain layers holding the same mix of fossil plants and animals. What can a geologist conclude?

options.label: The two cliffs were once a single cliff
The layers can be matched as the same age
The fossils were carried there by people
The lower cliff must be the younger one

items.explain: Strata from widespread locations containing the same fossil fauna and flora are said to be correlatable in time.

items.prompt: Tiny magnetic grains settle through water and are buried in mud. How does the mud end up recording Earth's ancient magnetic field?

options.label: The mud becomes magnetic from sunlight
Lightning magnetizes the buried grains
The grains line up with the field and burial fixes them
The grains slowly rotate to face north forever

items.explain: Very fine magnetic grains act like tiny compasses as they fall through water, lining up with Earth's field, and burial preserves that orientation.

items.prompt: Samples from a layer show that, when it formed, the North Magnetic Pole sat near the South Rotational Pole. How is that layer described?

options.label: Normal polarity
A stratigraphic hiatus
Lateral continuity
Reversed polarity

items.explain: Strata formed when the North Magnetic Pole was near the South Rotational Pole exhibit reversed polarity; normal polarity matches today's field.

items.prompt: Before radiometric dating was developed, what kind of scale was the 19th-century geologic time scale?

options.label: A relative scale of order
An exact scale in years
A scale based on sea levels
A scale of magnetic flips

items.explain: The geologic time scale stayed a relative scale until radiometric dating supplied an absolute time framework, leading to chronostratigraphy.

items.prompt: A run of rock layers has a stretch of time missing from it. Which of these could explain such a gap?

options.label: A reversal of Earth's magnetic field
Fossils sinking into lower layers
A pause in sediment being laid down
The rock cooling faster than usual

items.explain: A gap or missing strata, called a stratigraphic hiatus, may result from a halt in the deposition of sediment.

items.prompt: Why does visible banding show up in a cliff of layered rock?

options.label: Each band marks exactly one year of time
Physical contrasts between rock types
Light reflecting at different angles
Magnetic grains clumping in stripes

items.explain: Variation in rock units, most obviously seen as visible layering, comes from physical contrasts in rock type, or lithology.
